# Command exit status

Successful CLI commands return exit status zero. Reported operation failures
return a nonzero status and a diagnostic on stderr, including configuration/path
queries, version reads/writes, ignore updates and initialization. Argument parsing
errors also return nonzero.

For example, a malformed `_proj.yml` makes `proj yml read --project demo` fail,
so a shell or frontend can stop instead of treating the diagnostic as success.
Failed Git staging, commits and GitHub creation propagate as initialization errors;
a failed remote inspection does not proceed to GitHub creation.

This defines success versus failure, not stable error codes, a JSON result schema
or a capability protocol. Diagnostics remain human-readable text. Commands may
perform work before failing; a nonzero status is not a rollback guarantee.
